subject: prd/implement-now
statement: When a configured review attempt is admitted, the executor shall mint fresh attempt-scoped attribution material only after the implementation worker has terminated and its resources are released and bind its non-secret proof to the obligation, attempt identity, proposal, and revision. The launched reviewer process shall return exactly one schema-valid completed report to the **review artifact broker**: the impl-review-owned host-side persistence adapter that performs `prd:impl-review/FR-6`'s medium-appropriate proposal write and returns the exact native receipt; implement-now shall invoke and verify through that boundary but shall neither publish the artifact itself nor redefine impl-review's artifact contract. The review path shall remain inactive and implementation shall not proceed unless the live impl-review contract and design explicitly authorize that host-side adapter to perform FR-6 on the reviewer program's behalf and expose exactly-one publication returning that receipt; absent or ambiguous performer authority, receipt capability, or exactly-once semantics requires a sibling impl-review amendment and design first. The executor shall mark the obligation verified only after exact-reading that receipted artifact and authenticating its launched-attempt proof against canonical obligation/attempt/receipt state whose producer-signing authority is unavailable to every implementation and reviewer child process and workspace; generic repository/ref write credentials shall never authorize canonical state. The code-host author is transport metadata, need not differ from the implementation identity, and shall not participate in verification; raw attribution material shall never enter the implementation charter, workspace, event stream, or repository; and process exit, output text, a pre-existing or worker-authored artifact without that fresh proof, replayed proof, malformed artifact, a different proposal/revision, or worker-substituted evidence state shall never establish completion.
rationale: the artifact is the goal object only if the impl-review persistence boundary publishes it and its protected receipt proves which fresh reviewer invocation produced it, independent of the account used to transport it; transport affordances cannot substitute for sibling-contract authority and capability
fit_criterion: sibling-contract inspection blocks implementation and activation when host-adapter performer authority, receipt-returning publication, or exactly-once semantics is absent or ambiguous; once explicit, the launched reviewer has no direct proposal credential and hands exactly one completed report to the impl-review-owned broker; one broker proposal write returns one native receipt and its exact launched-attempt artifact verifies under either the same or a different code-host author; implement-now contains no second publisher; syntactically valid comments prewritten by the implementation worker, copied across attempts, replayed across proposal/revision, not matching the receipt, or paired with attempted obligation/attempt/receipt-store mutation fail as `artifact_untrusted`; missing/malformed/stale artifacts fail as `artifact_unverified`; write/read transport failure is infrastructure; capability and secret-scan fixtures find no raw attribution material or canonical producer-signing authority in either child launch
